notes: Hardware message carries only src/dest CPU plus two 32-bit words

title: Mailbox v2 hardware send path
notes: Send writes only tdata0, tdata1 and tid; it does not copy shared buffers

title: Mailbox v2 FIFO partitioning
notes: Eight FIFO entries are split 2/3/3 across three CPU channels

title: Mailbox demultiplex between message and SMP command
notes: A zero length field selects the cross-core SMP command handler

title: Mailbox device-level init ownership
notes: Device init and FIFO config are performed only by CPU0; other cores enable their own channel

title: Mailbox two-level indirection
notes: FIFO transfers the address and length of a software message structure in shared RAM

title: Software slicing of SWAP shared memory
notes: Software statically splits SWAP into four channels times two remote CPUs times two directions times 128 bytes

title: Armino logical channel command layout
notes: mb_chnl_cmd_t is a header plus three parameters and may carry a payload pointer

title: BK7258 Mailbox interrupt source
notes: INT_SRC_MAILBOX is 63 in GROUP1; per-core enables are bit 31 of SYS_CPUx_INT_32_63_EN

title: CP shell transport binding
notes: CP binds LOG_DEV and CMD_DEV to UART when SYS_PRINT_DEV_UART is selected

title: AP shell transport binding
notes: AP binds LOG_DEV and CMD_DEV to Mailbox when SYS_PRINT_DEV_MAILBOX is selected

title: AP print port initialization condition
notes: The configured print port is initialized only under SYS_PRINT_DEV_UART, so UART_PRINT_PORT alone proves nothing

title: CP ap_cmd builtin
notes: ap_cmd is a CP builtin that strips the prefix and forwards one command

title: CP to AP command forwarding
notes: shell_cmd_forward wraps the command as MB_CMD_USER_INPUT over Mailbox

title: AP shell task affinity
notes: AP shell task is created with affinity -1, so it is one OS-level shell rather than one per core

title: AP per-core log prefix
notes: Core identity is rendered as a log prefix only and does not route commands

title: AP exception UART bypass
notes: Exception output goes directly to the dump UART, which is configured as UART0

title: RPMsg UART initialization and device registration
notes: Both sides must call uart_rpmsg_init; the tty node is registered before any RPMsg link exists

title: RPMsg UART endpoint binding condition
notes: The endpoint is created only when the remote CPU name matches the configured cpuname exactly

title: RPMsg UART disconnect gap
notes: Endpoint destroy does not call uart_connected, so no ENOTCONN or POLLHUP is reported and blocked readers are not woken

title: Serial blocking and timeout semantics
notes: O_NONBLOCK returns EAGAIN; read timeout requires SERIAL_TERMIOS with VMIN and VTIME in non-canonical mode

title: Console uniqueness and rpmsg_serialinit timing
notes: Only one console driver may be selected and console binding is fixed during initialization

title: up_putc under RPMsg console
notes: A reference port implements up_putc as an empty function, removing the non-RPMsg early output path

title: RPTUN notify and receive callback path
notes: notify is mandatory for sending and the registered callback drives vring checking on receive

title: Team CP console and NSH ownership
notes: CP sets nsh_main as init entrypoint and enables DEV_CONSOLE, so the existing nsh belongs to CPU0

title: Team UART0 console registration
notes: UART0 is registered as /dev/console and /dev/ttyS0 on the CP image

title: Team AP RPMsg NSH configuration
notes: AP defconfig selects standard nsh_main with RPMsg UART console while keeping physical UART0 owned by CP
